linkedin:
What if you could run the full Firebase Local Emulator Suite on a laptop with the speed of a native binary? Firenook 0.2.1 makes that possible.

The Rust‑based emulators complete a Firestore write in about 5 ms, roughly 40× faster than the official suite’s 208 ms. Memory usage peaks at 2.1 GiB, a ten‑fold drop from the 22.5 GiB seen with the Java implementation.

Startup and restart times improve dramatically as well. The classic suite needs around 30.8 seconds to reload persisted state, while Firenook restores the same data in just 0.59 seconds. A demo‑shop loading over a million documents and tens of thousands of users comes online in under a second.

“Running the emulators on any machine without a Java runtime is a game‑changer.”  

These gains free up resources for CI pipelines and enable tighter feedback loops during development, allowing more realistic integration tests without the usual overhead.

The numbers reflect measurements from the 0.2.1 release; real‑world results may vary with different workloads.

Would you replace your current emulator setup with Firenook?
